title: The Health screen lists each backup with its restore-proof state, and not-yet-checked never reads as proven
description:
BROWSER CHILD of task-1f994315fd164a789424349cb7bba4ca, filed by architect-dbe3631e 2026-09-07. That row's own DoD 4 authorises this split verbatim: "If this breaches the file ceiling, split the browser half into its own row named in dependsOn - do not ship a route nothing fetches."

WHY IT BREACHED. I measured the real cost of a daemon read route from the landed precedent rather than from the parent's estimate. task-509c6c16 (`/deployments/health/read`, commit 29f5d723) touched FIFTEEN source files for the daemon half ALONE - the parent row says six. Adding the durable record and the three-state mapping puts the parent at eighteen. The browser half does not fit beside it.

THIS ROW CLOSES THE CONSUMER EDGE, which is the parent's rail 2 ("a producer with no consumer edge is the gap this row exists to close") discharged rather than deferred. The parent lands the route and registers itself in the daemon's own UNCONSUMED_SERVED_ROUTES census with a comment naming THIS ROW as the consumer that retires it; this row retires that entry and the UNPROXIED_SERVED_PATHS entry in the same edit. Both live in `apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.test.ts` (:129 and :174), so this row edits one daemon test file - that is expected and is how the census is designed to close.

THE ONE PROPERTY THIS ROW EXISTS FOR: NOT-YET-CHECKED MUST NEVER RENDER AS PROVEN. A backup that was written but whose restore check has not run is common - the write is cheap and the check is not - and an operator leans on that difference at the worst possible moment. Three states, visually distinguishable by more than colour, asserted SEPARATELY and by VALUE.

MEASURED AT HEAD 4710d60b (re-measure before planning; global rail 6):
- `apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts` - every read path is pinned here; a new read without its pin is not reachable in the dev lane.
- `apps/control-room/src/live/live-deployments-health.ts` is the exact-key decoder sibling to copy; the `live-*.ts` directory is the convention.
- `apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/environments-section.tsx` renders the Health screen section and is already wired through `live-environments.tsx` and LiveHealth, so no new mounting is needed - measure that claim before relying on it.
- The parent's served shape is whatever task-1f994315fd lands. Read it off disk; do not restate it here and do not mint a second spelling.

NOT IN SCOPE: the durable record, the three-state mapping, the route and its composition (all task-1f994315fd), and anything that changes what the daemon serves. If the served shape does not carry what this screen needs, report blocked against the parent rather than decoding around it.
definitionOfDone: AN EXACT-KEY CLIENT DECODER beside `apps/control-room/src/live/live-deployments-health.ts` decodes the parent's served frame. It refuses an EXTRA key AND a MISSING key, each with the specific code asserted AND the layer that refused - not merely that decoding failed. A malformed frame fails closed rather than dropping the restore-proof state silently.

THE THREE STATES RENDER SEPARATELY AND ARE ASSERTED SEPARATELY - proven, failed, not yet checked - in the backups list in `apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/environments-section.tsx`, with the state in a `data-` attribute and the three distinguishable by MORE THAN COLOUR (text or shape, so the distinction survives a monochrome or colour-blind reading). Assert each state's rendered output by value, never by a row count.

NOT-YET-CHECKED DOES NOT RENDER AS PROVEN, asserted as its own arm and DRILLED: make not-yet-checked render identically to proven and show the arm goes RED BY VALUE, not by a count. Quote the drill's failing line and its restore proof. This is the row's one safety property; an arm that only counts rows passes the mutation.

A BACKUP WITH NO SHA256 AND NO CHECK TIME RENDERS HONESTLY - absent is stated as absent, never as an empty string, a zero, a dash that reads as a value, or a defaulted 'proven'. Assert the absent case separately from the present one.

THE TWO CENSUS ENTRIES ARE RETIRED IN THE SAME EDIT: the parent's path leaves `UNPROXIED_SERVED_PATHS` (http-listener-read-dispatch.test.ts:129) and `UNCONSUMED_SERVED_ROUTES` (:174), and the comment the parent left naming this row goes with them. A separate arm greps those comments, so a half-retirement reds.

NO SECRET, CREDENTIAL, CONNECTION STRING OR RAW PATH THAT LEAKS ONE reaches the decoder, the rendered output, a log line, an error path or a committed fixture (epic rail 3). Assert it on a FAILURE path, with a positive control over a literal containing a credential shape so the arm cannot pass vacuously.

ASCII-only sources and apostrophe-free JSX text (the scheduler package-boundary scan reds on an apostrophe in JSX); confirm any new testid namespace is free before using it, following the sibling section's existing convention.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` (this row edits one daemon test file to retire the census), plus `pnpm typecheck`. A bare root `pnpm test` covers NO apps/** file and is not evidence here.
taskRails: NOT-YET-CHECKED IS NEVER PROVEN. That collapse is the entire failure this surface exists to prevent. Assert it by value and drill it.
READ THE PARENT'S SHAPE OFF DISK, DO NOT RESTATE IT. task-1f994315fd owns the served frame, its state vocabulary and its refusal codes. A second spelling in the browser is how the two drift apart.
DECODE EXACT-KEY, FAIL CLOSED. An extra key and a missing key each refuse with a code AND a layer; never drop an unknown member silently and never substitute a default for an absent one.
DO NOT CHANGE WHAT THE DAEMON SERVES. If the frame lacks what the screen needs, report blocked against the parent rather than decoding around it or minting the value client-side.
RETIRE BOTH CENSUS ENTRIES TOGETHER WITH THE PARENT'S COMMENT. Half a retirement leaves a served route recorded as unconsumed while a screen consumes it.
ASCII-ONLY SOURCES, APOSTROPHE-FREE JSX TEXT, dev-proxy-paths pin for the read.

implementationPlan.description: THE EXACT-KEY DECODER, copying the sibling's idiom rather than inventing one. New module in `apps/control-room/src/live/` beside `live-deployments-health.ts`, following its shape: an own-enumerable `exactDataRecord` snapshot at EVERY nesting level, module-scoped `LAYER` and `*_RESPONSE_INVALID` constants of its own (the sibling's are `CONTROL_ROOM_DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH` / `DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH_RESPONSE_INVALID` at :16-17), and a `refusalFrom` covering EVERY refusal envelope the parent's route can actually answer with — the sibling decodes THREE and its comment records that omitting the third is how a store refusal arrives with its cause erased, so read the parent's refusal shape rather than assuming two. Carry the null-vs-unreadable discipline from :159-165: each nested decoder answers null for both an absent and a malformed member, and the raw member is re-checked at the top, so a MALFORMED backup row can never read as an ABSENT one. Do NOT mint distinct codes for extra-key versus missing-key; both funnel to the module's one invalid-response code, which is what task rail 3 asks for.

- `exactDataRecord` copied VERBATIM from live-deployments-health.ts:100-121 (prototype check, ownKeys count-and-membership, per-key enumerable data-descriptor check, null-prototype snapshot, frozen). Applied at EVERY nesting level: the top-level frame ["backups","ok"] and each backup row ["checkedAt","environment","ref","restoreProof","sha256"].

- `refusalFrom` covers ALL THREE envelopes the route can actually answer with, each verified at its mint site in step 1, NOT assumed: {code,layer} (listener, refuseRequest), {code,layer,outcome:"REFUSED"} (route's BackupsReadRefused), {code,layer,ok:false} (the restore-proof STORE's BackupRestoreProofRefusal, layer DAEMON_INGRESS, which backups-read.ts:207-209 passes through verbatim). The third is exactly the one the sibling's comment warns about; omitting it would deliver a store refusal as a generic invalid response with its cause erased. The authenticator's five-key HttpRefused/HttpPortRefused are deliberately not matched, same as the sibling, and the module comment says so and why.

ONE CODE FOR BOTH MALFORMATIONS, per the step's instruction and task rail 3: extra-key and missing-key both funnel to invalidResponse() = errored(BACKUPS_RESPONSE_INVALID, CONTROL_ROOM_BACKUPS). The module comment records that what distinguishes the two arms is the OUTCOME (fail closed, no partial frame, no decoded backup), not the code - which is what step 3 asserts.

NULL-VS-UNREADABLE, placed where it actually applies. An array ELEMENT has no absent case, so `backupOf` returning null means unreadable only and `mapBackupsAnswer` refuses the WHOLE frame rather than dropping the row (a silently shorter list reads as "these are all the backups"). The real absent/malformed distinction is one level down on `sha256` and `checkedAt`, and `nullableText` carries it: null is admitted, "" is REFUSED. That is DoD 4's fail-closed direction - an empty string cannot arrive wearing the shape of an absent digest, and 0 is not a string so it refuses too.

DERIVES NOTHING (task rail 4). `restoreProof` is admitted against the daemon's exact three literals and copied; there is no default, no `??`, no mapping and no fallback anywhere in the module. A frame whose restoreProof is unreadable refuses.

EPIC RAIL 3 STRUCTURALLY: every failure exit returns invalidResponse(), built from module constants, carrying nothing off the wire - no partial list, no echoed request bytes. MAX_BACKUPS = 20000 mirrors the daemon's own read guard as a CRASH guard (an unbounded array is a render that never returns), documented as such rather than as a copy of daemon policy.

No test file yet - step 3 writes the arms.

implementationPlan.description: THE DECODER ARMS, WRITTEN SO THEY ARE NOT ONE ASSERTION TWICE — DoD 1. Both the EXTRA-key and MISSING-key cases will share the module's single code and layer, so asserting `status === "ERROR"` twice proves one thing twice. Each arm asserts the specific CODE and the LAYER (never merely that decoding failed) AND, crucially, that the decode FAILED CLOSED BY VALUE: no partial frame survives, no backup row is returned, and no restore-proof state leaks through. Add an arm per nesting level, since an extra key on a nested backup row is the likelier real defect than one at the top. Add the absent-member arms DoD 4 needs at this layer too: a malformed member must not read as an absent one. Then DoD 6's secret arm — on a FAILURE path, assert that no credential, connection string or secret-shaped literal reaches the decoder's output or its error value, and give it a POSITIVE CONTROL by running the same instrument over a literal that DOES contain a credential shape, so an arm that matches nothing cannot pass as an arm that found nothing.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 3 — THE DECODER ARMS. New apps/control-room/src/live/live-backups.test.ts, 22 arms, ALL GREEN: `Test Files  1 passed (1) / Tests  22 passed (22)`.

WHY THEY ARE NOT ONE ASSERTION TWICE (DoD 1, and the `risks` section's central warning). Extra-key and missing-key DO share BACKUPS_RESPONSE_INVALID @ CONTROL_ROOM_BACKUPS, so `expectFailedClosed` asserts four independent clauses that fail DIFFERENTLY: (1) status ERROR; (2) the CODE; (3) the LAYER that refused - this client's own, so a daemon layer here would mean a refusal envelope matched and the shape check was never reached; (4) FAIL-CLOSED BY VALUE - `Object.keys(outcome).sort()` is exactly ["code","layer","status"], `not.toHaveProperty("backups")`, and the SERIALIZED outcome contains none of "PROVEN", "NOT_CHECKED", "FAILED" or ".sqlite". Clause 4 is what a leaky decoder trips while 1-3 stay green.

ARMS PER NESTING LEVEL, as the step required: extra key at the TOP level; missing key at the TOP level; extra key on a NESTED backup row; missing key on a NESTED backup row; unknown restoreProof ("OK" and null) refused rather than defaulted; non-200; ok:false; backups not an array; null body.

DoD 4 AT THE DECODER LAYER - malformed never reads as absent: "" digest and "" checkedAt REFUSE (not folded to absent); 0 digest and numeric checkedAt refuse; `undefined` member refuses (which a missing key would otherwise mimic); ONE unreadable row refuses the WHOLE frame, never a silently shorter list. The present case is asserted separately from the absent one: backups[2] has sha256 null AND checkedAt null with restoreProof NOT_CHECKED, backups[1] has sha256 null but a real checkedAt, backups[0] has both.

THREE REFUSAL ENVELOPES, each asserted with BOTH its code and the layer that refused - listener {code,layer} -> LISTENER_BACKUPS_UNAVAILABLE @ CONTROL_ROOM_LISTENER; route {code,layer,outcome} -> BACKUPS_READ_CAPABILITY_DENIED @ CONTROL_ROOM_LISTENER; STORE {code,layer,ok:false} -> BACKUP_PROOF_STORE_UNAVAILABLE @ DAEMON_INGRESS. The third arm is the one that proves a store refusal does not arrive with its cause erased.

DoD 6 SECRET ARM WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL. `credentialShapesIn` runs six named patterns over the serialized value. POSITIVE CONTROL asserts by VALUE, not by non-emptiness: the poisoned frame yields exactly ["connection-string","userinfo-at-host","absolute-posix-path"]; a private-key header yields ["private-key-header"]; "DATABASE_PASSWORD is unset" yields ["password-token"]. NEGATIVE arm: the same instrument over the decoder's FAILURE-path output yields [], plus explicit not.toContain on the planted password and host. A vacuous instrument returns [] and reds the control immediately, so the arm cannot pass by matching nothing.
GOTCHA FOUND HERE: `/\bpassword\b/iu` does NOT match `DATABASE_PASSWORD` - `\b` does not fire after an underscore, which is a word character - so the boundary form would miss the commonest real leak shape. Widened to /password/iu and the reason is in the source comment.

A THROWN READ IS A FAILED READ, NEVER AN EMPTY ONE: the rejection handler settles `{code: BACKUPS_READ_FAILED, layer: CONTROL_ROOM_ENVIRONMENTS, status: "ERROR"}` rather than an empty list, so "no backups exist" is never said without knowing it. planningNotes.risks:
THE TWO MALFORMED-FRAME ARMS WILL SHARE ONE CODE AND ONE LAYER, so they are near-duplicates and one added layer away from vacuous — the exact shape global rail 1 warns about. Their distinguishing power CANNOT come from the code. It must come from asserting FAIL-CLOSED BY VALUE: after an extra key and after a missing key, the decoder yields the failure and NO partial frame — specifically, no backup row and no restore-proof state survives into the rendered output. An arm that only asserts `status === "ERROR"` twice proves one thing twice.

THE ROW'S ONE SAFETY PROPERTY IS A MUTATION TARGET, not a rendering preference. NOT-YET-CHECKED rendering as PROVEN is the collapse the surface exists to prevent, and DoD 3 requires the drill. Because the three states will share a row shape, a count-based arm survives the mutation — the DoD says so outright. Assert each state's rendered output BY VALUE (the `data-` attribute and the visible text), and make the drill red a NAMED arm by value.

MORE THAN COLOUR is a correctness requirement here, not styling: the distinction has to survive a monochrome or colour-blind reading, so text or shape carries it and the test asserts that carrier — a CSS class name alone is not a distinction a reader can see.

THE SECRET ARM CAN PASS VACUOUSLY, which is why DoD 6 demands a positive control: assert the absence of credential-shaped material on a FAILURE path, and prove the instrument works by running it over a literal that DOES contain a credential shape. Without the control, an arm that never matches anything looks identical to an arm that found nothing (`mem:gotcha-a-widening-grep-needs-a-positive-control`).
